sections.h2: Where do Lewis County, Kentucky owners go about a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share one address in Vanceburg. Both sit at 112 Second Street, one in Suite 101 and the other in Suite 102, which makes it easy to settle a question about value and a question about payment in the same trip.

Lewis County tax offices in Vanceburg
OfficeWhat it doesLocationPhone
Property Valuation AdministratorAppraises real property, handles exemptions and address changes112 Second Street, Suite 101606-796-2622
Lewis County SheriffMails and collects the current-year bill for the state, county and school districts112 Second Street, Suite 102606-796-2912
Lewis County ClerkTakes over delinquent bills and hosts the appeal filingVanceburg, the county seatListed on the clerk's website

The sheriff's office also collects for special districts such as fire protection and libraries where they exist. The PVA's office page stresses what it does not do: it writes no laws and sets no rates. Those belong to the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, and the PVA only assigns value. A PVA staffer or deputy must look at every parcel at least once in four years, and state law lets the office measure a building's exterior even when nobody is home.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Lewis County itself?
sections.html:
Lewis County sits on the Ohio River in the northeastern tip of Kentucky, and its river frontage is the longest of any county in the state. Across the water are Adams and Scioto counties in Ohio, and Greenup, Carter, Rowan, Fleming and Mason counties fill in the Kentucky side. The land rises from 485 to 1,400 feet above sea level, and its forested hills produced some of the country's best oak lumber.

The county was formed on December 2, 1806 from Mason County and named for Meriwether Lewis. The seat has moved twice: Poplar Flat held it first, Clarksburg from 1809 to 1863, and Vanceburg since. Vanceburg and Concord are the only cities, Garrison is the one census-designated place, and Tollesboro, Kinniconick and Laurel are among the many small communities. By the Census Bureau's 2020 count, every resident lived in a rural area.

The county's school system runs four elementaries, in Vanceburg, Garrison, Tollesboro and Laurel, plus a middle school and a high school beside KY 10, the AA Highway. Tollesboro's own high school closed in 1994, a closure that stirred real controversy at the time. The county profile counts 814 jobs in health care and social assistance, 680 in construction and 600 in manufacturing, so lumber is no longer the lead.

  • Mean travel time to work: 38.6 minutes.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $96,000, with 79.2 percent of homes owner-occupied.
  • Median rent: $751, and median household income: $46,838.
  • Population estimate for July 2025: 12,901, a 1.4 percent dip from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: How does the Lewis County sheriff want the bill paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page gives three routes. You can mail the stub and a check to 112 Second Street, Suite 102, Vanceburg, KY 41179, pay in person at the office, or pay by debit or credit card over the phone or at the counter. Cards carry a convenience fee that scales with the size of the bill. Make checks out to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office, write the property ID from the bill on the check, and never mail cash.

Pay only the single figure in the "If Paid By" box at the bottom right of the bill. The subtotals for each taxing jurisdiction are shown for information, and separate payments for each would only cause confusion. A returned check costs $25, and the late schedule on the bill still applies when you resend. Overpayments are refunded after a phone call and some documentation, and one payment may cover several bills if you enclose every stub.

Statute sets the calendar. Paying in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the face amount is due through December 31, January adds 5 percent, and later payment adds 10 percent. The sheriff's bill lists the exact amounts for each date, so follow the schedule printed on your own statement.

sections.h2: What happens when a Lewis County tax bill goes unpaid past April?
sections.html:
The sheriff's list moves to the clerk after the close of business on April 15, and the debt becomes a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and clerk and attorney commissions are added.

The Department of Revenue's worked example uses a $1,000 bill. Paid within five business days of reaching the clerk, it costs $1,387.79 once interest, the clerk's commission and the lien fee are added, and the county attorney's fee is waived. Wait for the first attorney notice and the same bill costs $1,611.30. Under a normal schedule, the sale to third-party purchasers falls between July 14 and August 28, because state law sets it 90 to 135 days after the transfer.

Omitted property works differently. A bill for property that was left off the roll, or for a value raised after an appeal, is due the day it is prepared, and a further 10 percent applies if it sits for a full month.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Lewis County assessment?
sections.html:
First request a conference with the PVA or a deputy. The law requires it before any appeal, and it must occur before or during the public viewing period.

That viewing period lasts 13 days and opens on the first Monday in May. If you met with the PVA, the clerk accepts your appeal until the close of the next workday after viewing ends. Kentucky's board of assessment appeals must convene at the county seat, so Lewis County cases are heard in Vanceburg, between 25 and 35 days after the viewing period ends.

  • The board hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA present, so plan to attend or send an authorized representative.
  • Useful evidence includes photos, insurance policies, construction costs, an appraisal, and nearby listings or sales.
  • You may record the hearing, and the PVA may do so only after written notice to you.
  • Skipping the board forfeits any later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Who gets the Lewis County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Homeowners aged 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, qualify when the home is their residence. The deduction for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100, applied to the assessed value before the rates are applied.

The sheriff's page points applicants to the PVA at 606-796-2622. Only one exemption is allowed per household even if both spouses qualify, and a mobile home classed as real property or a manufactured house can count as the residence. Whoever buys the house must apply again in their own name, and the owner who sold must report the transfer to the PVA.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when a Lewis County house sells?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page says the seller usually pays a prorated share at closing for the part of the year they owned the house, and the buyer then pays the entire bill when it arrives. Read the settlement statement to confirm. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still lets the owner see the bill, and the owner stays legally responsible for it.

The bill is sent to whoever owned the property on January 1, unless a deed filed afterward carries specific tax bill instructions for the current year. The county clerk also collects the state transfer tax of 50 cents per $500 of value when the deed is recorded, and the statute exempts transfers made through foreclosure, between divorcing spouses, or from parent to child for nominal consideration. If a tax bill is delinquent, expect the title agent to require a payoff from the sheriff or the clerk before funds are released.

faqs.q: What number do I call about a Lewis County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff at 606-796-2912 about payment, and the PVA at 606-796-2622 about value or exemptions. Both offices are at 112 Second Street in Vanceburg.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Lewis County tax with a card?
faqs.a: Yes. The sheriff takes debit and credit cards over the phone or at the office and charges a convenience fee based on the bill's size. Checks go to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office with the property ID written on them.

faqs.q: What does a bounced check cost in Lewis County?
faqs.a: The fee is $25, and the late-payment schedule printed on the bill still applies when you send a replacement payment. Pay the amount for the date your funds actually arrive.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage lender handle the Lewis County bill?
faqs.a: Often, but you still receive a copy and remain legally responsible. If you think escrow covers it and you are unsure, ask the lender, and ask the sheriff if the bill is missing.

faqs.q: Who pays when I sell my house in Lewis County?
faqs.a: The settlement statement decides, and sellers usually cover a prorated share for the months they owned the house. The buyer then pays the whole bill when it comes, and any delinquent amount has to be paid for clear title.
